pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #11
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Percussion instruments make sound when they are (1 mark)
   A. blown with air only
   B. sung into
   C. struck, shaken or scraped
   D. bowed with a stick of hair

2. To make a very dark tone with charcoal you should (1 mark)
   A. use water
   B. use no charcoal
   C. press very lightly
   D. press harder

3. In an overhead pass, the ball starts (1 mark)
   A. behind the knees
   B. between the knees
   C. above the head
   D. at the ankles

4. What is the length of a full netball court? (1 mark)
   A. 30.5 metres
   B. 100 metres
   C. 10 metres
   D. 50 metres

5. What do the letters GK stand for? (1 mark)
   A. Goal King
   B. Goal Kicker
   C. Great Kicker
   D. Goal Keeper

6. Which position takes the centre pass to start the game? (1 mark)
   A. GD
   B. GK
   C. GS
   D. C, Centre

7. The game restarts after each goal with (1 mark)
   A. a jump ball
   B. a centre pass
   C. a throw-in from the side
   D. a penalty kick

8. Why should you take turns to talk about each other's work? (1 mark)
   A. To waste time
   B. So no one speaks
   C. To make others sad
   D. It is fair and respectful

9. When darkening a colour with black, you should add (1 mark)
   A. a whole tin at once
   B. nothing
   C. a little at a time
   D. white first

10. What is a good way to blend the edges of two tones? (1 mark)
   A. With a knife
   B. With sand
   C. With a dry stone
   D. With a damp brush

11. A coil of clay is (1 mark)
   A. a long thin roll like a snake
   B. a flat sheet
   C. a plate
   D. a hard brick

12. A melody is (1 mark)
   A. the beat of a drum
   B. the loudness
   C. the tune of a song
   D. the words only

13. Leaning far backwards while sprinting will (1 mark)
   A. make you jump
   B. make you faster
   C. make no difference
   D. slow you down like a brake

14. A relay race is a race in which (1 mark)
   A. people throw a ball
   B. one person runs all the way
   C. team members take turns running and pass a baton
   D. people jump into sand

15. On the Kenyan flag, green stands for (1 mark)
   A. the people
   B. the sun
   C. the rivers only
   D. the land and natural wealth

16. A roll in gymnastics is (1 mark)
   A. a song
   B. a run
   C. a movement in which the body turns over along the floor
   D. a still position

17. Where should you place your hands in a crab balance? (1 mark)
   A. Behind you, shoulder-width apart
   B. On your head
   C. In your pockets
   D. In front of your face

18. A sign that narrows to the right means (1 mark)
   A. getting softer
   B. getting louder
   C. repeat
   D. getting faster

19. Singing in unison means (1 mark)
   A. nobody sings
   B. everyone sings different tunes
   C. only one sings
   D. everyone sings the same notes at the same time

20. A song about washing hands to prevent germs is a (1 mark)
   A. marriage song
   B. funeral song
   C. naming song
   D. topical song

21. The lens of a camera (1 mark)
   A. stores photos
   B. keeps it cool
   C. lets light in
   D. gives power

22. Which hand is at the top of the recorder? (1 mark)
   A. Neither
   B. Left
   C. Both feet
   D. Right

23. For a good tone you should blow (1 mark)
   A. gently and steadily
   B. as hard as you can
   C. only in short puffs
   D. with your cheeks puffed for ever

24. How many joints does a descant recorder have? (1 mark)
   A. Five
   B. Three
   C. Six
   D. Two

25. A squeaky, very high sound usually means you are (1 mark)
   A. playing a drum
   B. blowing too hard
   C. holding it upside down
   D. blowing too gently

26. Water games help learners to (1 mark)
   A. study more
   B. feel comfortable in the water
   C. forget to swim
   D. avoid the pool

27. Which Kiswahili word means frog? (1 mark)
   A. kaa
   B. twiga
   C. chura
   D. tembo

28. The crab walk strengthens the (1 mark)
   A. arms, shoulders and tummy
   B. eyes
   C. ears
   D. hair

29. Which of these is a national day on which the anthem is sung? (1 mark)
   A. Market day
   B. Birthday of a friend
   C. Jamhuri Day
   D. Sports day only

30. In a folk song, the chorus (1 mark)
   A. paints
   B. answers and repeats
   C. conducts the umpire
   D. hides

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Describe how to do the side roll safely. (4 marks)

32. Explain how to prepare and perform a folk song with your class. (5 marks)

33. Why should a short melody end on d? (2 marks)

34. Name three types of Kenyan folk songs and say when each is sung. (3 marks)

35. State the jobs of the lens, the screen and the battery of a camera. (3 marks)

36. Why do we use a streamlined shape when gliding? (2 marks)

37. Name four guide lines used for free hand lettering. (4 marks)

38. How should you receive feedback from others? (3 marks)

39. State the length of a crotchet and of a quaver in beats. (2 marks)

40. What does it mean to improvise a rhythmic pattern? (3 marks)

41. What is a balance in gymnastics? (2 marks)

42. State three values taught by the Kenya National Anthem. (3 marks)

43. Give four safety rules for sprint races. (4 marks)

44. Describe how to play an animal game safely and fairly from warm-up to the end. (5 marks)

45. Describe how to make an overhead pass. (3 marks)

46. Explain how to make a shade of green. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #11 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — struck, shaken or scraped
   A percussion instrument is played by hitting, shaking or scraping it.

2. D — press harder
   Pressing harder leaves more charcoal, so the tone is darker.

3. C — above the head
   The ball is lifted above the head before it is thrown.

4. A — 30.5 metres
   A full court is 30.5 metres long and 15.25 metres wide.

5. D — Goal Keeper
   GK is the Goal Keeper, a defender who guards the goal.

6. D — C, Centre
   The Centre takes the centre pass.

7. B — a centre pass
   The game restarts with a centre pass, and the teams take turns.

8. D — It is fair and respectful
   Taking turns shows respect and love for others.

9. C — a little at a time
   Black is strong, so add it in small amounts.

10. D — With a damp brush
   A damp brush joins the tones smoothly.

11. A — a long thin roll like a snake
   A coil is a long, thin, even roll of clay.

12. C — the tune of a song
   A melody is a series of notes that make a tune.

13. D — slow you down like a brake
   Leaning back acts like a brake.

14. C — team members take turns running and pass a baton
   In a relay, runners pass a baton to the next teammate.

15. D — the land and natural wealth
   Green stands for the land and its natural wealth.

16. C — a movement in which the body turns over along the floor
   A roll turns the body over along the mat.

17. A — Behind you, shoulder-width apart
   Hands go behind you, about shoulder-width apart.

18. A — getting softer
   A closing sign means the music grows softer.

19. D — everyone sings the same notes at the same time
   Unison means the same notes together.

20. D — topical song
   It gives a message about a topic of importance.

21. C — lets light in
   The lens gathers light for the picture.

22. B — Left
   The left hand is at the top and the right hand at the bottom.

23. A — gently and steadily
   A gentle, steady breath gives a warm tone.

24. B — Three
   Head joint, middle joint and foot joint.

25. B — blowing too hard
   Gentle air makes a good tone.

26. B — feel comfortable in the water
   They build confidence.

27. C — chura
   Chura is a frog.

28. A — arms, shoulders and tummy
   The body is held up by the arms and legs.

29. C — Jamhuri Day
   Jamhuri Day is a national holiday.

30. B — answers and repeats
   The chorus responds to the soloist.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: Lie on the back with body straight. Stretch the arms overhead with palms together and legs together. Tighten the tummy and point the toes. Roll over on to the side and tummy in a straight line. Get up slowly.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid step.

32. (5 marks)
   Answer: Choose a song and say the community, type and message. Share roles among soloist, chorus and instrumentalists. Practise pitch, rhythm, tempo and dynamics. Add gestures and expressions. Perform with respect and take a bow.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for choosing the song, roles, practising, expression and performing respectfully.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: d is the home note. Ending on it makes the melody sound finished.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each idea.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: Work songs during work, funeral songs when someone dies, naming songs when a baby is named, initiation songs at initiation, marriage songs at weddings, worship songs at worship. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each type with its occasion.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: The lens lets light in; the screen shows the view and photos; the battery gives power.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: A long, thin shape slips through the water easily, so you glide further.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: Ascender line, top of small letters, baseline and descender line.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each line.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Listen quietly, do not argue, say thank you and think about the ideas.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: A crotchet is one beat and a quaver is half a beat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: To make up a pattern on the spot without writing it first, using an instrument such as a drum or shaker to keep to the beat of a song.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for making up on the spot, 1 mark for no writing first, 1 mark for using an instrument.

41. (2 marks)
   Answer: A position held still for a few seconds under control.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for still position, 1 mark for control or holding.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Unity, peace, justice, hard work, service, patriotism and thankfulness to God. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Run in your own lane; check the track for stones; wear proper clothes; never push or trip; slow down gradually after the finish; warm up. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: Warm up and choose soft clear ground. Explain the rules and roles. Play the game without pushing or pulling. Stop at the whistle and give everyone a turn. Cool down and drink water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each stage.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Lift the ball above the head with both hands and elbows slightly bent. Step forward and throw from behind the head, flicking wrists and fingers so the ball goes over the defender.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the start, 1 mark for the throw, 1 mark for going over the defender.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: Add a small amount of black to green, and more if needed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for black, 1 mark for adding a little.
